info.name: Melissa Data API
info.description:
This collection contains ready-to-use request templates for Melissa’s suite of cloud-based data quality APIs. Use these templates to quickly validate, cleanse, and enrich addresses, names, emails, phone numbers, and more—without the need to manage local reference data.

Key features:

- Sample requests for all major Melissa APIs
    
- Organized folders by API category for easy navigation
    
- Designed for rapid testing and integration
    

How to use:

1. Fork this collection to your workspace
    
2. Add your API key as an environment variable
    
3. Send requests and view real-time responses
    

Resources:

- 📚 Full API documentation: [https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/cloud-api.html](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/cloud-api.html)
    

All reference data is securely maintained on Melissa servers, ensuring you always access the most up-to-date information.

item.description:
Personator™ Cloud Service provides CASS/DPV certified Address Verification and optionally leverages comprehensive Consumer data for all-in-one email, phone, name checking, name to address verification, move update, and appending missing information, demographics, enrichments.

View full service documentation [here](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/personator-consumer/personator-consumer-index.html).

item.name: Global Address

query.description: Transmission Reference: Unique and arbitrary identifier that will be returned unmodified.
Customer ID (License Key): Authorization string issued by Melissa.
Organization: Organization name associated with the address record.
Address Line 1: Input field for the address. This should contain the delivery address information (house number, thoroughfare, building, suite, etc.)
Address Line 2: Additional delivery address information.
Address Line 3: Additional delivery address information.
Address Line 4: Additional delivery address information.
Address Line 5: Additional delivery address information.
Address Line 6: Additional delivery address information.
Address Line 7: Additional delivery address information.
Address Line 8: Additional delivery address information.
Double Dependent Locality: Smallest population center data element. Depends on Locality and DependentLocality.
Dependent Locality (US = "Urbanization") : Smaller population center data element. This depends on the locality element.
Locality (US = "City"; Canada = "Municipality"): Most common population center data element.
Sub Administrative Area (US = "County"): Smallest geographic data element.
Administrative Area (US = "State"; Canada = "Province"): Most common geographic data element.
Sub National Area: Administrative region within a country on an arbitrary level below that of the sovereign state.
Postal Code (US = "ZIP"; Canada = "Postcode"): The complete postal code for a particular delivery point.
Country: Country name, abbreviation, or code.
Format: Desired format of the response; JSON or XML

item.description:
SSN Name Match determines if the Social Security Number is within the acceptable range, and matches against the First and Last Name.

In addition, the Cloud API will also check if the SSN is flagged as deceased.

You can use SSN Name Match to:

- Verify SSN syntax is correct
    
- Verify the SSN exists
    
- Match First and Last Name to the SSN
    
- Perform deceased suppression based upon SSN
    

Learn more about SSN Name match on our docs page: [https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/ssn-name-match/ssn-name-match-index.html](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/ssn-name-match/ssn-name-match-index.html)

item.description:
Welcome to the People Business Search Cloud API by Melissa. Search, verify and correct consumer and business data across millions of records through its powerful search engine.

People Business Search can be used to:

- Search for individuals and businesses across the US.
    
- Perform searches with partial/limited information on the address, name or company to correct records that would otherwise be unresolvable.
    
- Locate individuals for billing purposes, such as tracking down people who have skipped out on their bills.
    
- Validate policyholder addresses before issuing policies, to reduce the risk of fraud and errors.
    
- Find potential customers by targeting your marketing campaigns to specific locations.
    
- Retrieve contact phone information for an individual or business.
    

Learn more about People Business Search on our docs page: [https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/people-business-search/people-business-search-index.html](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/people-business-search/people-business-search-index.html)

item.description:
Melissa Releases allows users to securely and efficiently download data files, object binaries, and other collateral files from Melissa.

This service enables users to automate the process of updating their data by allowing them to script the download of specific files rather than downloading the entire zip file.

Additionally, file versioning is provided, making it easier to download historical data if necessary.

Parameters for Melissa Releases are primarily path parameters. Therefore the values used become part of the URL path in the requests and should be used in a specific order.  

To learn more about Melissa Releases, vist our documentation: [https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/cicero/cicero-index.html](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/cicero/cicero-index.html)

**COLS** parameter:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| @record | Row's unique identifier |

| @transaction | Name of the alert or transaction |

| @resultCodes | Result codes associated with the alert |
| @description | Description of the transaction |
| @highlightColor | Index of color to use to highlight record |
| @highlightColumns | Which columns should be highlighted |
| @alertType | Type of alert (PostalUpdate, ChangeOfAddress, etc) |

| @moveType | Type of move (when applicable) |
| @dateOfDeath | Date of death (when applicable) |

**@transaction** and **@transactionColumns** pseudo-columns will be used.

## WhereCondition

The **WHERE** parameter can contain a T-SQL compatible WHERE expression that will filter selected  
records. Columns used in **WHERE** do not need to appear in **COLS**. If used simultaneously with the  
**KEYS** parameter, the **JoinCondition** option can be used to specify whether both (**And**) or  
either (**Or**) properties must be satisfied in order for a record to be returned.

## Options

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KeysAre@Records | bool | false | If **true**, then records having the same **@record** as the specified PrimaryKey(s) will be selected |

## TransactionOrder

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| EarliestToLatest | Transactions are ordered from earliest to latest(default) |
| LatestToEarliest | Transactions are ordered from latest to earliest |
| LatestThenEarliest | Transactions are ordered with the latest first, followed by the remainders ordered earliest to latest |

request.description:
It may be necessary to call **GetFileInfo** several times to get a full analysis of a file. For example,  
if the file is a compressed file, the first call would return with **FileFormat** set to **Compressed**,  
and a list of the compressed files in **CompressedFiles**. A second call would specify which file to  
analyze in the compressed file parameter. If the compressed file is an Excel spreadsheet, this call  
would return **FileFormat** as **Excel**, and **Sheets** would contain a list of the sheets in the Excel  
file. Finally, a third call would be made with the input file, compressed file and sheet name parameters  
specified. This call would finally return **SampleData** and **Records**.

Regardless of **FileFormat** or **Delimiter**, the records returned in **SampleData** will be tab-delimited.

## Options

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LimitRows | int | 10 | Limit the number of rows to return |
| TrimWhitespace | bool | true | Trim leading and trailing spaces from text data |
| Delimiter | string | null | Delimited file format delimiter |
| CorrectColumnNames | bool | true | Automatically correct minor column naming issues |

By default, **GetFileInfo** will analyze the specified file and determine the file's format (Delimited,  
JSON or Excel) and, in the case of the **Delimited** format, the column delimiter. However, this can be  
overridden by specifying **FORMAT** and the **Delimiter** **OPT** property.

To learn more visit [File.](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#file)

request.description:
## PrimaryKeys

If multiple Primary Keys are to be deleted, list them in the body's **PrimaryKeyValues** property. If  
the table does not have a primary key, the records' [@record](#description/selection-columns) value should  
be used. The **KeysAre@Records** option can be used to use **@record** when the table does contain a  
primary key but deletion by **@record** is desired.

## Options

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KeysAre@Records | bool | false | If **true**, then records having the same **@record** as the specified PrimaryKey(s) will be deleted |
| AbortOnAnyError | bool | true | If **true**, then a data or rule issue on any record will cause the entire set of records to not be updated |
| AbortOnErrors | string | "" | Only abort if any record reports a result code in the specified (comma-delimited) list of result codes |
| LimitErrors | int | 10 | Maximum number of errors reported in **Results** (0 for none, -1 for all) |

To learn more visit [Record](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#record).

response.name: DeleteRecords

request.description:
This function offers three different ways of providing insert data:

- **Dictionary-based** - Records are contained in a **List**<**Record**\>, where **Record** is JSON  
    representation of the table's schema. This is the method shown in this Swagger document.
    
- **Delimited Records** - Records are contained in a **List**<**string**\>, where each list element  
    is a delimited record.
    
- **Key/Value Pairs** - Records are contained in a **List**<**List**<**InsertRecord**\>>, where  
    **InsertRecord** is a key/value pair.This interface is very similar to how requests are done in the  
    HubSpot API.
    

## Options

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CreateTable | bool | false | If **true**, a non-schema table will be created if the specified table doesn't exist |
| ReplaceExistingRecords | bool | false | If **true**, then an existing record having the same primary key will be entirely replaced with the input record |
| UpdateExistingRecords | bool | false | If **true**, then an existing record having the same primary key will be updated with the input record |
| AbortOnAnyError | bool | true | If **true**, then a data or rule error reported on any record will cause the entire set of records to not be inserted |
| AbortOnErrors | string | "" | Only abort if any record reports a result code in the specified (comma-delimited) list of result codes |
| BypassAllRules | string | "" | Bypass any validation of business rules |
| BypassRules | string | "" | Bypass validation of specified business rules (comma-delimited list) |
| Delimiter | string | "Comma" | For the **Delimited** Records request type, which delimiter is used to delimit fields (**Tab**, **Comma**, **Pipe**, **Colon** or **Semicolon**) |
| LimitErrors | int | 10 | Maximum number of errors reported in **Results** (0 for none, -1 for all) |
| TransactionType | string | "Insert" | Transaction type |

## Column Mappings

By default, column names in the input records must match column names in the table schema. If  
the input columns do not match the table schema, the **ColumnMappings** property can be used  
to define the mapping between input columns and table columns. Only mappings that differ from  
the table schema need to be specified.

To learn more visit [Record](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#record).

request.description:
Update records are identified by the primary key, which must be specified for each record . If the table  
does not have a primary key, the records' [@record](#description/selection-columns)  
value should be used. If both are present, **@record** will be used.

Data can be formatted:

- **Delimited**
    
- **JSON** (one row of JSON per record or as a giant List)
    
- **Excel**
    

See [Asynchronous Processing](#description/asynchronous-processing) for details.

## Actions

- **Update** - Existing data will be updated with data in the upload file. Column data in the existing record  
    that does not exist in the upload file will remain.
    
- **Replace** - Existing data will be replaced in it's entirety with the data in the upload file. Column data in  
    the existing record that does not exist in the upload file will be removed.
    
- **Delete** - The specified columns in the upload file will be removed from the existing data (the values are  
    ignored). Columns in the existing record that do not exist in the upload file will remain.
    

## Options

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AbortOnAnyError | bool | true | If **true**, then a data or rule issue on any record will cause the entire set of records to not be updated |
| AbortOnErrors | string | "" | Only abort if any record reports a result code in the specified (comma-delimited) list of result codes |
| DeleteInputFile | bool | false | If **true**, then the upload file will be deleted after a successful operation |
| SkipRows | int | 0 | Skip a number of rows at the top of the input file |
| LimitRows | int | 0 | Limit import to a specific number of rows (0 means all rows) |
| TrimWhitespace | bool | true | Trim leading and trailing spaces from text data |
| Encoding | string |  | For the **Delimited** file format, the upload file's encoding (ie, "ASCII", "UTF-8", "windows-1252", etc). If not specified, the encoding will be auto-detected. |
| Delimiter | string | "Comma" | For the **Delimited** file format, which delimiter is used to delimit fields (**Tab**, **Comma**, **Pipe**, **Colon** or **Semicolon**) |
| FirstRowSchema | bool | false | For **Delimited** and **Excel** file formats, **true** indicates that the first row of data contains the schema. If both **FirstRowSchema** and **COLS** are specified, this option takes precedence |
| CorrectColumnNames | bool | true | Automatically correct minor column naming issues (if **FirstRowSchema** is specified) |
| LimitErrors | int | 10 | Maximum number of errors reported in **Results** (0 for none, -1 for all) |
| TransactionType | string | "Update" | Transaction type |

## Notes

- Compressed files must have one of the following extensions: **7z**, **bz2**, **gz**, **gzip**,  
    **lz**, **rar**, **tar** or **zip**
    
- Excel files must have one of the following extensions: **xls** or **xlsx**
    
- When the upload file is a compressed file archive and the compressed file name is not specified, then  
    the archive must contain only a single file -or- a file having the same name as the table name.  
    Otherwise, an error is returned.
    
- When the upload file is an Excel spreadsheet and the sheet name is not specified, then the spreadsheet  
    must contain only a single sheet containing data -or- a sheet having the same name as the table name.  
    Otherwise, an error is returned.
    

To learn more visit [Record (FTP Async)](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#record-ftp-async).

Endpoints in this folder support FTP-based record operations executed asynchronously. These requests allow records to be inserted, searched, selected, updated, or deleted while providing process-level status tracking. This folder is designed for large or long-running FTP operations that require non-blocking execution.

request.description:
AlterTable can be used to add, replace, update or delete a table's columns. **ColumnName** and  
**NewColumnName** dictate the action to be taken:

| ColumnName | NewColumnName | Type/Size/PrimaryKey | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Specified | Same as **ColumnName** | Same as current schema | No changes made to column |
| Specified | Same as **ColumnName** | Not same as current schema | Column's schema altered |
| Specified | Not same as **ColumnName** | Same as current schema | Column renamed |
| Specified | Not same as **ColumnName** | Not same as current schema | Rename column and alter column's schema |
| Empty or NULL | Specified | Specified | Add column with the specified schema |
| Specified | Empty or NULL | (n/a) | Delete column |

The same logic is used for **Rules** (**RuleName**), **Jobs** (**JobName**), **Alerts**  
(**AlertName**) and **Notifications** (**NotificationName**). **Tags** are always replaced in entirety.

To learn more visit [Table](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#table).

item.description:
Endpoints in this folder are used to retrieve record-level transaction history within the Vault. These requests allow you to inspect transaction details associated with record operations.

To learn more please visit our documentation: [https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#transaction](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-reference-guide.html#transaction)

Vault is a cloud-based DBMS. In addition to the functionality found in other cloud-based DBMS services, the Vault can provide scheduled processing using the same tools that Melissa offers on other platforms.

Vault parameters include path parameters. These path parameters become part of the URL path in the requests and should be used in the specific order.

With the exception of a few endpoints, Vault requires authentication tokens as a header parameter, not as a request parameter.

To learn more about the Vault API, visit our documentation: [https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-index.html](https://docs.melissa.com/cloud-api/vault/vault-index.html)
